doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Studio years, bass choir and bass philosophy
title: Artists he recorded with: Dinah Washington, Quincy Jones, Aretha Franklin, Judy Garland
summary: Hinton lists Dinah Washington's Mercury sessions, Quincy Jones's first dates, first Mathis, Jackson and Franklin dates, and Judy Garland at Carnegie Hall.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well you certainly earned it. With a lot of the freelance things that you were discussing earlier, who were some of the people that you recorded with over the years, some that just jump out? I mean it would be impossible to name everybody.

Well some of them that were really important that I did quite a bit with… most of Dinah Washington‟s stuff with Mercury, most of that stuff. Quincy Jones first dates. I‟ve got some of them. If you have a moment I‟d like you to see. Quincy sent me for my birthday when he couldn‟t come to Town Hall… he sent something that… you know what we were about.
But I did the first Johnny Mathis dates, the first Mahalia Jackson dates, the first Aretha Franklin dates, Barbra Streistan‟s Funny Girl. The Record Of The Year, what‟s the name…
No, not Natalie Cole. What‟s the great white singer, a woman singer, her daughter‟s a singer now. Liza Minellia.
I did her mother‟s Record Of The Year at Carnegie Hall.
